newsitem.title: USA: FX mkts eye key technicals for EMU turmoil-experts.
newsitem.headline: FX mkts eye key technicals for EMU turmoil-experts.

text.p: The Socialist Party's victory in French parliamentary elections on Sunday is likely to trigger foreign exchange volatility with market players trying to push currencies past key technical levels, experts said.
"This gives speculators more to work with now. There'll be a lot of guesses, and certainly a lot of speculations," said Goldman, Sachs International vice chairman Robert Hormats.
Hormats was referring to the Socialists' plan to move away from the fiscal austerity needed to meet the European Monetary Union (EMU) debt criteria and promote growth instead.

"This creates in the mind of the market the view that the Euro will not be as strong a currency as was anticipated," added Hormats who predicted that lax fiscal policies and calls for high-yielder countries to be in the Euro from its planned January 1, 1999, start will pressure European currencies.
"A lot of European money will go into the Swiss franc and in other non-EMU currencies," said Hormats, referring to the British pound, the U.S. dollar and the yen.
Senior analyst Chris Turner at I.D.E.A., a consultancy firm, said one major uncertainty for foreign exchange markets is the parity at which the Euro would start trading.
"The level talked about in Paris is one (Euro)-to-one (U.S. dollar), meaning a 40-percent devaluation of the Euro (compared to current European/U.S. forex rates)," Turner said.

"We can expect a lot more pressure on French (market) interest rates and see how the government is going to stand up to that," added Turner who predicted "the French franc is going to suffer. Maybe the speculators will look for another cross than mark/Paris, like dollar/Paris."
Mark/Paris broke through 3.3835 -- a key level that I.D.E.A. technical analysts said paves the way for a push to 3.4015 -- soon after the elections' results.
Among other key technical levels, I.D.E.A. chartists cited:

-- DOLLAR/MARK which is moving toward very strong resistance at 1.7120 -- the 62-percent retracement from 1.7389, the high on April 28, to 1.6680, the low on May 12. The next resistance levels are at 1.7165, then 1.7210, and 1.7389, the top of the range.

-- DOLLAR/YEN, little affected by the European situation, retains strong support at 115.30. Resistances are 117.00 and 117.85/90, the 38-percent retracement between 111.88, the low on May 20, and 127.47, the May 1 high.
-- MARK/YEN, reflecting the pressure on the European currencies, is heading lower for a test of key support at 67.90, a double-bottom.
-- MARK/SWISS, in similar situation, broke through support at 0.8270. Next support is at 0.8220.
-- STERLING/MARK confirms strength of non-EMU European currencies versus EMU candidates. Move from low of 2.7512 in last week of May to 2.8015 on Friday points to attack on key resistance at 2.8055.
-- DOLLAR/SWISS FRANC breaking resistance at 1.4170 pegged to dollar's push through 1.7120 marks.
